Calculate \(\epsilon\) threshold for spatial clustering

Source: R/get.epsilon.R
get.epsilon.Rd

Computes the threshold \(\epsilon\) (epsilon) based on step lengths. The threshold can be calculated using density curve intersections (requires a behavioral state column with exactly two states), or simply by calculating the overall mean or median of the step lengths. The calculation can be applied globally, per individual, or per group.

Usage

get.epsilon(
  data,
  state.col = "state",
  step.col = "step",
  mode = "global",
  method = "density",
  ids = NULL,
  group.col = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame or an object of class disperseR containing movement data.

state.col

Character. The name of the column containing the behavioral states. Only used and required if method = "density". Must contain exactly two unique states for the evaluated subset. Default is "state".

step.col

Character. The name of the column containing the step lengths. Default is "step".

mode

Character. The level at which to compute the threshold: "global", "individual", or "groups". Default is "global".

method

Character. The method used to calculate the threshold: "density" (intersection of density curves for two states), "mean", or "median". Default is "density".

ids

Character. The name of the column containing individual identifiers. Required if mode = "individual".

group.col

Character. The name of the column containing group identifiers. Required if mode = "groups".

Value

A numeric value representing the threshold if mode = "global", or a named list of numeric thresholds if mode = "individual" or mode = "groups".

Examples

# Intersection of the step-length densities of both states
get.epsilon(sim_states)
#> Computing a global threshold using all data combined.
#> [1] 238.4065

# One threshold per individual, using the median step length
get.epsilon(sim_states, mode = "individual", ids = "ID", method = "median")
#> Computing thresholds separately for each individual.
#> $F02
#> [1] 43.78989
#> 
#> $F04
#> [1] 36.19222
#> 
#> $F05
#> [1] 42.71265
#> 
#> $M01
#> [1] 35.1432
#> 
#> $M03
#> [1] 40.90247
#>
